# WageTheft.law

> California wage theft lawyers. Unpaid overtime, missed meal and rest breaks, off-the-clock work, late final paychecks, misclassification and PAGA claims, for one worker or a whole crew. Free case review.

WageTheft.law is operated by Centurion Trial Attorneys, APC, a California employment law firm. Attorney responsible: Ryan Stygar. Phone: 1-888-CALL-RYAN.

## Guides
- [Can My Employer Round My Time Punches or Auto-Deduct My Lunch in California?](https://wagetheft.law/articles/time-rounding-auto-deducted-meal-breaks-california/): California allows time rounding only if it doesn't shortchange workers over time. Meal punches can't be rounded, and auto-deducts can hide unpaid work.
- [What Happens If My Employer Doesn't Give Me Breaks in California?](https://wagetheft.law/articles/meal-and-rest-breaks-california/): Missed a meal or rest break in California? You may be owed an extra hour of pay for each day. Here are the break rules and how far back you can recover.
- [Am I Misclassified as an Independent Contractor in California?](https://wagetheft.law/articles/misclassified-independent-contractor-california/): California presumes you're an employee unless your company passes all three parts of the ABC test. Learn the warning signs and what you can be owed.
- [Is It Legal to Make Me Work Off the Clock in California?](https://wagetheft.law/articles/off-the-clock-work-california/): No. California employers must pay for security checks, pre-shift meetings, after-hours texts and work done after clocking out. Here's what you can recover.
- [When Is My Final Paycheck Due in California?](https://wagetheft.law/articles/final-paycheck-waiting-time-penalties/): Fired, laid off, or quit in California? Here's when your final paycheck is due, what it must include, and how waiting time penalties add up.
- [What Is PAGA in California, and How Does It Work?](https://wagetheft.law/articles/paga-explained/): PAGA lets one California worker recover Labor Code penalties for the whole crew. Who can file, the LWDA notice, the one-year deadline and how penalties split.
- [When Do I Get Overtime in California?](https://wagetheft.law/articles/unpaid-overtime-california/): California overtime starts after 8 hours a day or 40 a week, with double time after 12. How it's calculated, how employers dodge it, and how far back to claim.
